observations: The page number «91» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. At the foot, the signature «12*» on the right. L01: «wandschaft» completes «keine grosse Ver-» at the end of p. 90 (JP2 0122, L37); see the critical note. L01-L08: «Im ersten Werke», the Sūrya-Siddhānta, «im zweiten Werke», the Pañcasiddhāntikā (p. 90, L36-L37); the rule of the second is quoted in German quotation marks.
L09-L10: the heading of chapter 34, in bold, centred, with the reference to the text below it; «77a», the a raised. L11: «Die Regel Kh.’s … sind»; see the critical note.

L23: the formula, displayed and centred, its fraction built up, written {fr:NUMERATOR|DENOMINATOR}, the comma after it set apart; z, h and the letters of the figure in italics, «sin», «cos» upright, «·» the raised dot of multiplication.

A figure stands at the right of L24-L38, which are set in a narrower measure at its left; it is not reproduced. A circle, the meridian, with Z at its top, P at the upper right, E at the upper left, H at the left end and T at the right end of a horizontal dashed diameter, K at the lower right; dashed lines: the vertical diameter from Z, the diameter H T, the diameter from E through the centre to K, and a diameter from P through the centre to the lower left. Solid arcs: the horizon from H to T, curving down through A and B; the ecliptic from E through M and B to K; the circle of altitude from Z through M to A, marked z between Z and M and h between M and A; the arc from M to P; the angle at M between M E and M Z marked with a small arc. The letters are italic.

L21-L38. Checked: the triangles E H B and M A B have right angles at H and A, where the meridian and the circle of altitude meet the horizon, and the common angle at B between the ecliptic and the horizon; by the rule of four quantities (p. 61, JP2 0093, L10) sin EH : sin EB = sin B = sin MA : sin MB, so that sin h = sin MA = sin EH · sin MB : sin EB, and cos z = sin h, z = 90° − h. P being the pole of the ecliptic, the arc M P stands at right angles to the ecliptic, so that the angle Z M P is the complement of the angle E M Z, as L37 says. N01. Checked: 8 miles of about 1973 m (p. 43, JP2 0075, L12) are 15.8 km, «c. 16000 Meter».

L03: the ö of «Himmelskörper» is printed with the left side of its o missing, so that it looks like a reversed c with the two dots; read as ö. L26: «gibt. EH ist die Ekliptikhöhe, aus der Dekli-», the words set close in the narrow measure. L29: «finden ;», the semicolon after a thin space (11 px).

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Kh.», «Batt.», «Nallino»; italics: «Yojanas», «Parallaxen», «Zenitdistanz z», the letters of the formula and the figure, «Medium Coelum», «Aszendenten B,» (L31; «Aszendenten.» upright in L32), «Winkel», «Breite», «Länge,», «Yojana».
The other colons and the semicolon stand after the thin space of the edition (10-15 px measured; «die Regel :» in L05, 15 px).
